canonical.title: What a BFF costs you every day: OpenAPI codegen and the local dev loop

parent.title: Pure React 19 SPA or a .NET 10 BFF? A decision framework for an internal admin console

siblings.title: In-memory tokens vs cookie-backed BFF sessions under XSS: what each architecture actually buys you
siblings.summary: httpOnly cookies do not stop XSS — they convert silent token exfiltration into loud, tab-bound session riding. That's a real but bounded win; CSP + Trusted Types is the actual mitigation.

siblings.title: Does the IETF browser-based-apps BCP apply to an internal admin console?
siblings.summary: The BCP names "business applications" in its strongest recommendation, so an internal console is in scope — but the ranking is a security/simplicity trade-off, not a normative MUST.

siblings.title: Refresh tokens and silent renew in a browser SPA (2026)
siblings.summary: Iframe silent renew is dead cross-site but alive same-site; refresh-token rotation works on both stacks, DPoP only really works on Keycloak, and TanStack Query needs a single-flight mutex either way.

siblings.title: Greenfield BFF vs retrofitting later: where the asymmetry actually is
siblings.summary: Adding a BFF later is a two-way door — if you build the SPA with one auth module, one fetch wrapper, relative paths and no client-side JWT parsing. The one-way door is the API, not the frontend.

siblings.title: BFF options in .NET 10: Duende.BFF, YARP, or hand-rolled
siblings.summary: If you build a BFF, the realistic .NET 10 choice is YARP + AddOpenIdConnect + the free Apache-2.0 Duende.AccessTokenManagement (~250 LOC you own), or Duende.BFF if you qualify for its free Community Edition; Duende.BFF's paid entry point is $5,750/yr.

sources.title: Duende BFF — UI hosting
sources.claim: Same-origin hosting of UI and BFF means the auth cookie is sent automatically and no CORS headers are required.

sources.title: Duende — Managing OpenAPI specifications with BFF and Swagger UI
sources.claim: A BFF requires transforming downstream OpenAPI specs: rewrite paths and servers, merge documents, strip security schemes, add an X-CSRF request interceptor.

sources.title: Duende BFF — Remote API endpoints
sources.claim: MapRemoteBffApiEndpoint maps a local BFF path onto a remote API address and forwards sub-paths; all such endpoints require an x-csrf header.

sources.title: Duende BFF — /bff/user endpoint
sources.claim: The /bff/user endpoint returns session claims plus bff:logout_url and bff:session_expires_in; 401 when anonymous; requires X-CSRF: 1.

sources.title: Duende BFF — Samples
sources.claim: Duende ships official BFF samples for OpenAPI, YARP integration, and Separate Host for UI.

sources.title: web.dev — Understanding same-site and same-origin
sources.claim: A 'site' is scheme + eTLD+1; the port is not part of it. http://localhost and https://localhost are cross-site.

sources.title: Vite — Server options (server.proxy)
sources.claim: Reverse proxies in front of Vite must proxy WebSocket, else the HMR client falls back to connecting directly to the Vite HMR server.

sources.title: Wrapt — Standalone Duende BFF for any SPA
sources.claim: A working standalone Duende BFF + Vite setup proxies four route groups: /bff, /api, /signin-oidc, /signout-callback-oidc, with secure:false.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — OpenAPI support in ASP.NET Core 10
sources.claim: .NET 10 defaults to OpenAPI 3.1, supports YAML output (not at build time), and build-time generation via GetDocument.Insider.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — Customize OpenAPI documents
sources.claim: Document transformers have access to the entire OpenAPI document and can mutate it.

sources.title: Swagger — Cookie authentication
sources.claim: Cookie authentication is not supported for 'try it out' requests due to browser security restrictions.

sources.title: DZone — Swagger UI in a BFF architecture
sources.claim: Swagger UI is a public client that injects bearer tokens and bypasses cookies/CSRF, which a secure BFF rejects.

sources.title: microsoft/kiota-typescript — issue 1817
sources.claim: Kiota's TypeScript client has no built-in way to configure fetch options, so credentials:'include' requires a hand-written fetch function.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — Kiota authentication
sources.claim: Kiota provides an AnonymousAuthenticationProvider that performs no operation, for APIs that don't require a token.

sources.title: openapi-fetch — API reference
sources.claim: createClient accepts baseUrl plus any valid fetch option, so cookie auth is a two-line change.

sources.title: RicoSuter/NSwag — issue 5229
sources.claim: NSwag's WithCredentials = true does not emit credentials into the generated Fetch-template TypeScript client.

sources.title: NSwag — TypeScriptClientGenerator wiki
sources.claim: NSwag exposes UseTransformOptionsMethod, requiring a transformOptions method that receives and returns RequestInit.

sources.title: Orval — Documentation
sources.claim: Orval supports an output baseUrl and an override.mutator custom fetch/axios instance.

sources.title: Hey API — Fetch client
sources.claim: Hey API's createClient accepts baseUrl, headers and credentials.

sources.title: .NET Blog — New Aspire app with React
sources.claim: AddViteApp puts the Vite dev server in the app model and injects the API address so vite.config.js builds server.proxy, eliminating CORS.

sources.title: InfoQ — Aspire 13.2 released
sources.claim: Aspire 13.2 (March 2026) closed 1,100+ issues, themed on the CLI, TypeScript AppHost preview, and seamless local development.

sources.title: Code with Mukesh — Aspire for .NET developers deep dive
sources.claim: Aspire pays off with multiple communicating services, but adds unnecessary overhead for a single API plus a database.

sources.title: andreytreyt/yarp-swagger
sources.claim: YARP has no built-in OpenAPI aggregation; this extension reuses YARP cluster/route config to publish an aggregated Swagger document.

sources.title: Duende BFF — Third-party cookies
sources.claim: Browsers increasingly block third-party cookies, so SameSite=None is not a safe workaround for split-host dev.

sources.title: liuweiGL/vite-plugin-mkcert
sources.claim: vite-plugin-mkcert generates a locally-trusted CA and certificates for Vite's HTTPS dev server.

sources.title: jmelosegui — .NET dev cert with Vite
sources.claim: The ASP.NET Core dev certificate can be exported as a PFX and fed to Vite so both dev servers share the HTTPS scheme.

sources.title: microsoft/aspire — Roadmap Q1 2026 update
sources.claim: The Aspire Q1 2026 roadmap confirms active investment in the CLI, TypeScript AppHost and local development experience.
